contributions.text: 9. What steps she is taking with Cabinet colleagues to ensure safe and accessible transport to school for pupils.
contributions.name: Sarah Edwards

contributions.who: The Parliamentary Under-Secretary of State for Education (Paul Waugh)
contributions.text: Local authorities must make safe, suitable and free travel arrangements for eligible children. Buses and coaches are regulated as public services vehicles and are expected to meet high safety standards. Licensing authorities are also expected to ensure that taxis and private hire vehicles are safe and roadworthy, and that their drivers are fit and proper.
contributions.name: Paul Waugh
contributions.role: The Parliamentary Under-Secretary of State for Education

contributions.text: It is the 33rd anniversary of the M40 school minibus tragedy, in which 12 children and their teacher lost their lives. I extend my condolences to all those affected. Exemptions remain in the law that allow unqualified and untrained staff or teachers to drive a school minibus, when other drivers would normally be required to have a D1 licence. Despite assurances in February from Department for Education and Department for Transport Ministers that they would meet to address the licensing exemption, no action has so far been taken, and these section 19 permits continue to put the safety of children at risk. I recently heard a report of a school minibus leaking brake fluid for weeks, because there is no set minibus inspection for schools. The official guidance for minibuses is 13 years out of date. Will the Minister please take action on this matter, or do we need to wait for another tragedy?
contributions.name: Sarah Edwards

contributions.text: May I, too, extend my condolences to all those marking that anniversary? I commend the tireless campaigning by my hon. Friend and by Liz and Steve Fitzgerald, who have done so much to raise the public profile of this important matter. What happened to their daughter and the other children involved was, indeed, a terrible tragedy. I know my hon. Friend has met the Minister for School Standards who agreed to work with the Department for Transport to understand the impacts of changing the regulations. I will of course be happy to meet my hon. Friend to update her on how those conversations are progressing, but she can rest assured that the Government are fully engaged with the campaign and her calls for changes to minibus driver licensing.
contributions.name: Paul Waugh
contributions.role: The Parliamentary Under-Secretary of State for Education

contributions.text: Those who attended my recent school and college transport roundtable with Cornwall council and colleges across Cornwall were absolutely exasperated with the rising costs. SEND children in Cornwall have to travel double the distance of their peers in England, and Cornwall council has said that its transport budget will hit £44 million by 2028-29. Will the Minister consider introducing rural adjusted funding formulas to offset these higher transport costs in rural areas?
contributions.name: Ben Maguire

contributions.text: As my hon. Friend the Minister has already set out, the entire purpose of this Government’s SEND reforms is to make sure that we address the situation for every child with every need, and that includes transport. We can get those bills down, particularly where there is mainstream education and an education closer to where parents want, rather than having to send children out of the area.
contributions.name: Paul Waugh
contributions.role: The Parliamentary Under-Secretary of State for Education
